items.79514: Suzhou's historic center is a "water town" – think {start_bold}idyllic canals lined with lanterns{end_bold} and crossed by {start_bold}antique bridges{end_bold}, with the {start_bold}pagodas of old temples{end_bold} hanging overhead.
items.213835: Rhodes' old town is one of the {start_bold}largest preserved medieval city centers{end_bold} in Europe. It's all gray stone and ancient inscriptions, with picturesquely named streets like {start_bold}"Avenue of the Knights."{end_bold}
items.20015725: San Diego was the site of the first Spanish settlement in California. Strap on your cowboy hat and walk past {start_bold}original adobe houses{end_bold} and {start_bold}old-timey saloons{end_bold} for an authentic Western experience.
items.20023904: The highlight of St. Augustine’s old town is the view over {start_bold}Matanzas Bay{end_bold}. Explore the old fortress walls inside the 300-year-old {start_bold}San Marcos Castle{end_bold} as well as the interesting collections in the {start_bold}Lightner Museum{end_bold}.
items.20083006: Albuquerque’s {start_bold}Old Town Plaza{end_bold} comes to life with music and dancing. All around it, shops stay busy and restaurants serve up {start_bold}New Mexican cuisine{end_bold} using ingredients like red-green chiles and black beans.
items.20111994: U.S. democracy was born in these cobblestone streets. Make sure to see national landmarks like {start_bold}Independence Hall{end_bold}, {start_bold}Betsy Ross's House{end_bold}, and the {start_bold}Liberty Bell{end_bold}.
items.20115955: Charleston is one of the oldest and most well-preserved cities in the United States. And it shows in this area's {start_bold}graceful Colonial architecture{end_bold}. Don't miss the distinctive {start_bold}"Pink House,"{end_bold} built in 1694.
items.20154335: Multicolored houses with balconys fill the sunny streets of San Juan’s old town. The arches of an {start_bold}impressive town hall{end_bold} overlook {start_bold}Plaza de Armas{end_bold}, with {start_bold}cafes{end_bold} scattered around it.
items.900000000: Jerusalem's ancient old town is sacred to three world religions. Taking center stage are the {start_bold}Western Wall{end_bold}, the {start_bold}Church of the Holy Sepulchre{end_bold}, and the {start_bold}Dome of the Rock{end_bold}.
items.900039384: Jutting out into the {start_bold}Adriatic{end_bold}, Budva’s old town is over {start_bold}2,500 years old{end_bold}. Get lost wandering its {start_bold}winding streets{end_bold} and past {start_bold}terracotta-topped buildings{end_bold}, then discover its history in the {start_bold}striking citadel{end_bold}.
items.900047975: Tbilisi's old town is full of {start_bold}ancient houses{end_bold} with ramshackle, {start_bold}brightly-painted wooden balconies{end_bold}. The area comes across as {start_bold}a mix between Cairo and Moscow{end_bold}.
items.900050223: {start_bold}Bai-style houses{end_bold}, known for their upturned eaves and marble finishes, are some of Dali Old Town’s main attractions. Original gates lead the way towards {start_bold}temples{end_bold} and {start_bold}markets{end_bold} selling beautiful calligraphy.
items.-101499: The streets in Zadar’s old town are paved with {start_bold}marble{end_bold} and lined with the remains of its {start_bold}Roman and Venetian history{end_bold}. Check out the {start_bold}Sea Organ{end_bold} – steps on the waterfront that make "music" when the water passes through pipes underneath.
items.-101579: {start_bold}Cobblestone streets?{end_bold} Check. {start_bold}Historic monuments?{end_bold} Check. But there's also a distinctive modern vibe to this old town – check out attractions like {start_bold}"The Museum of Broken Relationships."{end_bold}
items.-1045268: Architectural styles like Baroque and Neoclassical come together with medieval buildings in Lviv's old town. Enjoy its {start_bold}town hall and tower{end_bold}, then stop by {start_bold}St. George’s Cathedral{end_bold} which dates back to the 18th century.
items.-110164: Blending {start_bold}Catalan and Italian influences{end_bold}, Alghero’s old quarter is filled with {start_bold}Gothic architecture and bustling squares{end_bold}. Stop by one of its {start_bold}cafes{end_bold}, or wander through to the {start_bold}nearby marina{end_bold}.
items.-111255: Bari’s old town is known for its {start_bold}moat-encircled Norman castle{end_bold} and cobblestone streets that wind into a circular shape. Stop at the impressive {start_bold}Basilica San Nicola{end_bold} and {start_bold}San Sabino Cathedral{end_bold} as you explore.
items.-111474: Reached by funicular, Bergamo’s old town is enchanting. Pass through Piazza Vecchia to see the {start_bold}Duomo cathedral{end_bold}, before taking in sights like the {start_bold}Colleoni Chapel{end_bold} and {start_bold}Accademia Carrara Gallery{end_bold}.
items.-111742: Bologna old town’s {start_bold}terracotta rooftops and elegant basilicas{end_bold} watch over its {start_bold}portico-adorned squares and winding streets{end_bold}. Markets and restaurants showcase classic {start_bold}Emilia-Romagna dishes like tortellini{end_bold}.
items.-111758: The {start_bold}architecture{end_bold} in Bolzano’s old town is a pleasant blend of {start_bold}pastel-colored buildings, murals and elaborately finished arcades{end_bold}. Cobblestone streets are perfect for some {start_bold}al fresco dining and drinking{end_bold}.
items.-112463: Cagliari’s old town is a mix of {start_bold}ancient churches, towers, and palaces{end_bold}. Enclosed by the old city walls, it’s a treasure chest of {start_bold}museums home to medieval jewelry and Roman and Phoenician artifacts{end_bold}.
items.-113074: Caorle’s old town is right in between {start_bold}two beaches{end_bold}. In its heart, you’ll find the {start_bold}11th-century Santo Stefano Cathedral{end_bold}, with the beautiful seafront {start_bold}Madonna dell'Angelo’s bell tower{end_bold} acting as a lighthouse.
items.-114787: Some Baroque monuments in Catania's old town, nestled below {start_bold}Mount Etna{end_bold}, can claim a unique building material. That's not regular stone – it's lava.
items.-114960: Cefalù’s old town is nestled between a {start_bold}rock and a golden beach{end_bold}. Explore its {start_bold}11th-century cathedral{end_bold} before hiking up the rock to see the ruins of the {start_bold}Tempio di Diana{end_bold} and {start_bold}views of the sea{end_bold}.
items.-1153613: Brașov is a charming collection of candy-colored medieval houses, surrounded by the {start_bold}Carpathian mountains{end_bold}. Don't miss the colossal Gothic {start_bold}"Black Church"{end_bold} in the center of town.
items.-1153951: {start_bold}Hipsters{end_bold} and {start_bold}trendy clubs{end_bold} populate this colorful district, which managed to survive the twin ravages of World War II and communist-era city planning relatively intact.
items.-1156174: Cluj-Napoca old town’s architectural mix of {start_bold}Gothic{end_bold}, {start_bold}Baroque{end_bold}, and {start_bold}medieval{end_bold} styles fills this energetic student town. In the evening, you'll find {start_bold}bars{end_bold} and {start_bold}cafes{end_bold} that come to life.
items.-116052: A city of {start_bold}churches{end_bold} and {start_bold}celebrity-owned villas{end_bold}, all nestled by the crystal-clear waters of {start_bold}Lake Como{end_bold}.
items.-1170221: In Sibiu’s old town, you’ll find the remains of an {start_bold}old city wall{end_bold} and buildings with {start_bold}colorful, sloped roofs{end_bold}. The upper and lower towns are home to the main sights and charming squares.
items.-1170266: Small areas of brightly painted houses lining {start_bold}picturesque squares{end_bold} and {start_bold}cobblestone streets{end_bold} make Sighișoara's old town a feast for the eyes. You'll find treetops intertwined with steeples and a {start_bold}210-foot-high clock tower{end_bold}.
items.-1172411: Timişoara’s old town is full of impressive {start_bold}Secession architecture{end_bold}, giving it the nickname "Little Vienna." Several parks enhance the beauty of landmarks like the {start_bold}Orthodox Cathedral{end_bold} and {start_bold}Union Square{end_bold}.
items.-117387: Ferrara’s Renaissance old town is hidden behind 16th-century walls. Inside you'll find {start_bold}Estense Castle{end_bold}, {start_bold}San Giorgio Cathedral{end_bold}, and restaurants serving {start_bold}salama da sugo{end_bold} (sausage with potato and pumpkin mash).
items.-117543: This is Florence's famous center, where glories of the Renaissance like {start_bold}Michelangelo's {start_italics}David{end_italics}, Botticelli's {start_italics}Birth of Venus{end_italics}, and Brunelleschi's famous dome{end_bold} can be admired in pristine condition.
items.-118400: Walk the streets of the old city and you'll pass by {start_bold}Christopher Columbus' birthplace{end_bold}, not to mention endless {start_bold}elaborate palaces{end_bold} and {start_bold}one very ancient lighthouse{end_bold}.
items.-118729: Set on a peninsula surrounded by the Adriatic Sea, Grado’s old town is filled with {start_bold}shops{end_bold} and {start_bold}cafes{end_bold}. Make sure to stop at the {start_bold}Byzantine-era basilica{end_bold} to see its mosaics and frescoes.
items.-119920: The highly embellished front of the {start_bold}Basilica di Santa Croce{end_bold} gives some insight into Lecce old town’s elaborate architecture. Its narrow streets wind around pretty squares and past {start_bold}museums{end_bold}.
items.-120405: Lucca is known as the {start_bold}"city of 100 churches"{end_bold}, many of which you can see as you pass along the old city walls that encircle it. Within the walls, the {start_bold}Duomo cathedral{end_bold} and {start_bold}Guinigi Tower{end_bold} are the main draws.
items.-1204094: Macau's old town is an {start_bold}exotic mix of Portuguese and Chinese influences{end_bold}. The iconic facade of {start_bold}St. Paul's Cathedral{end_bold} is a must-see.
items.-120965: The rooftops of Mantova’s old town are decorated with countless cupulas and towers. Stop by {start_bold}Piazza Castello{end_bold} that’s lined with porticos and the vast {start_bold}Ducal Palace{end_bold} with its many courtyards and gardens.
items.-121381: Matera’s old town is an amazing network of cave houses, known as {start_bold}"sassi"{end_bold}. Bars, restaurants and hotels are built into the {start_bold}limestone rock face{end_bold} and you can take a walk through uninhabited caves.
items.-122902: This neighborhood of {start_bold}churches{end_bold}, {start_bold}catacombs{end_bold}, and {start_bold}ancient ruins{end_bold} is divided neatly in two by a charming, tourist-friendly avenue called the Spaccanapoli. The streets here still follow their ancient Greek outlines.
items.-123662: In the middle of Padova’s old town, {start_bold}Basilica di Sant’Antonio{end_bold} and {start_bold}Duomo cathedrals{end_bold} are loved for their decorative features. {start_bold}Piazza dei Signori square{end_bold} is a popular meeting place, with plenty of eateries and bars.
items.-123999: Parma’s old town is overflowing with gems, including {start_bold}Piazza Garibaldi square{end_bold} with its astronomical clock and the {start_bold}Romanesque Duomo cathedral{end_bold}. Stop by a piazza cafe to take in the buzz of the city.
items.-124324: Perugia’s old town packs in medieval streets, a cathedral, and Roman ruins. Uncover the area’s history in museums like {start_bold}Museo Archeologico Nazionale dell'Umbria{end_bold} and {start_bold}Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria{end_bold}.
items.-124352: Surrounded by Lake Garda and fortress walls, Peschiera del Garda’s old town has a unique feel. Pass through {start_bold}Porta Verona Gate{end_bold} and over {start_bold}Voltoni Bridge{end_bold} to discover {start_bold}Roman ruins{end_bold} and {start_bold}inviting restaurants{end_bold}.
items.-124918: Churches share the spotlight with museums and ancient botanical gardens in Pisa’s old town. Stop by {start_bold}Piazza del Duomo{end_bold} to get an unbeatable view of the city’s sights and the must-see {start_bold}Leaning Tower of Pisa{end_bold}.
items.-126693: Rome's city center is home to nearly {start_bold}three millennia of history{end_bold}. Walk in the shadows of the {start_bold}Colosseum{end_bold}, {start_bold}St. Peter's{end_bold}, and literally hundreds of other ancient monuments.
items.-127126: Salerno’s old town is full of trattorias serving up fresh seafood straight from the Amalfi Coast along with the famous {start_bold}lemon granita ice{end_bold}. Walk off your meal with a stroll past sights including the {start_bold}cathedral{end_bold} and {start_bold}Arechi Castle{end_bold}.
items.-127559: San Gimignano’s skyline is dominated by 14 extravagant {start_bold}towers{end_bold} dating back to medieval times. Take a walk through ancient streets to {start_bold}Palazzo Comunale{end_bold} and climb its 218 steps for unbeatable views.
items.-128201: Nicknamed "La Pigna" (the pine cone), Sanremo’s old town is a maze of arch-covered alleys winding their way towards the sky. {start_bold}Churches{end_bold}, {start_bold}gardens{end_bold}, and {start_bold}squares{end_bold} are perfect for scenic stops along the way.
items.-129709: Sprawling over three steep hills, Siena’s maze-like old town is set around {start_bold}churches{end_bold}, {start_bold}museums{end_bold}, and {start_bold}squares{end_bold} full of cafes. {start_bold}Torre del Mangia tower{end_bold} has the best views over the town and countryside.
items.-129785: {start_bold}Ancient ruins{end_bold}, an {start_bold}amphitheater{end_bold}, and {start_bold}elaborate chapels{end_bold} are some of the must-sees in Siracusa’s impressive old town. You'll also find a market and several trattorias serving up the city’s famous {start_bold}fish specialities{end_bold}.
items.-129795: Accessible only by {start_bold}castle drawbridge{end_bold}, Sirmione’s tiny old town sits on a small island in the middle of Lake Garda. This ancient "comune" is home to {start_bold}Castello Scaligero castle{end_bold} and the ruins of a {start_bold}Roman villa{end_bold}.
items.-130467: With a setting under Mount Etna, Taormina's old town features some {start_bold}dramatic views{end_bold} over the rolling hillside below. The highlight is its {start_bold}Greek amphitheater{end_bold} that sits serenely overlooking the sea.
items.-130938: Turin's old town, {start_bold}once the seat of kings{end_bold}, is appropriately grand and elegant. Don't miss the area's most famous attraction – the mysterious {start_bold}Shroud of Turin{end_bold}, located in the Cathedral of St. John.
items.-131189: Trapani's small, Baroque-era old town is a delight to wander around in. Don't miss the {start_bold}Ligny Tower{end_bold}, an old castle that juts dramatically out into the sea.
items.-131282: Piazza Duomo forms the hub of Trento’s old town, with restaurants and cafes surrounded by a {start_bold}Romanesque cathedral{end_bold}. Make your way through the surrounding streets to see incredible {start_bold}frescoes{end_bold} and {start_bold}porticoes{end_bold}.
items.-131346: A {start_bold}Romanesque basilica{end_bold} and the seaside {start_bold}Miramare Castle{end_bold} are just a few of the stars of Trieste’s old town. Start exploring at {start_bold}Piazza dell'Unità d'Italia{end_bold} and make a pit stop at a busy café.
items.-132007: Stay in the celebrated core of Venice, where you can ride a gondola through the {start_bold}world-famous canals{end_bold} or take a stroll through {start_bold}ancient alleyways{end_bold} – unchanged for hundreds of years.
items.-132092: Find a place in the charming center of Verona – the setting of {start_bold}Shakespeare’s {start_italics}Romeo and Juliet{end_italics}{end_bold}.
items.-1406939: Medieval and Roman ruins blend with narrow alleyways in Aix-en-Provence’s old town. Keep an eye out for {start_bold}fountains{end_bold}, {start_bold}picturesque squares{end_bold}, and {start_bold}an old belfry with an astronomical clock{end_bold}.
items.-1407760: Annecy’s old town is full of {start_bold}arcades{end_bold} with hidden boutiques and restaurants. The {start_bold}Palais de l’Île{end_bold} sits peacefully on one of the many canals that wind through the old quarter.
items.-1409631: Looking over the Rhône River, Avignon’s old town wraps around {start_bold}Palais des Papes palace{end_bold} and its courtyards. Make your way through the medieval streets and down to the "broken bridge," {start_bold}Pont Saint-Bénézet{end_bold}.
items.-1411193: {start_bold}Burgundy-style architecture{end_bold}, {start_bold}Gothic chapels{end_bold}, and {start_bold}Renaissance mansions{end_bold} dot the picturesque old town of Beaune. No visit to the region would be complete without a visit to the {start_bold}Burgundy Wine Museum{end_bold}.
items.-1416701: Carcassonne’s old town is an impressive medieval citadel overlooking the new town below. Cross the centuries-old {start_bold}Pont Vieux{end_bold} while you pass through mazelike streets leading to a {start_bold}castle{end_bold} and {start_bold}majestic city gates{end_bold}.
items.-1421049: A mix of {start_bold}canals{end_bold} and {start_bold}pastel-colored, wooden houses{end_bold} make up Colmar’s fairytale-like old town. During the Christmas season, you'll find it overflowing with holiday market stalls.
items.-1423981: Dijon’s old town sits in the shadow of {start_bold}Notre-Dame{end_bold}, its 13th-century cathedral protected by gargoyles. The main square, {start_bold}Place de la Libération{end_bold}, is as majestic as it gets and is home to the {start_bold}Palais des Ducs palace{end_bold}.
items.-1432206: Honfleur’s old town, Vieux Bassin, and its collection of colorful, waterfront houses appear in many {start_bold}Impressionist paintings{end_bold}. Explore galleries or enjoy the views from {start_bold}Notre-Dame de Grâce church{end_bold}.
items.-1438604: The fiercely independent and ancient seaport of La Rochelle is still guarded by {start_bold}stunning fairy-tale towers{end_bold} – perfect for a city locals call {start_bold}"belle et rebelle“{end_bold} (beautiful and rebellious).
items.-1447079: Lille's fascinating old town offers a {start_bold}unique mix of French and Belgian architecture{end_bold} – you might be a little unsure about which country you're in, but you'll be charmed regardless!
items.-1448468: Lyon's old town is crisscrossed by {start_bold}"traboules"{end_bold} – hidden passageways built in the Middle Ages, where merchants could transport goods without going out into the street.
items.-1449947: Le Panier ("the Basket") is {start_bold}a maze of narrow alleys{end_bold}, {start_bold}ateliers{end_bold} (workshops), and {start_bold}cafes{end_bold}. It gets its name from the ancient Greek marketplace it was built on.
items.-1450921: Menton’s oceanside old town is full of colorful buildings and gardens leading up to the Baroque {start_bold}Basilica of Saint-Michel{end_bold}. Be amazed at the views from up here, or wander down to the {start_bold}19th-century market{end_bold}.
items.-1453260: Fall in love with Montpellier's old town, full of {start_bold}quiet squares{end_bold} and {start_bold}grand hôtels particuliers{end_bold} with beautiful courtyards.
items.-1454990: Nice's old town is full of {start_bold}quaint, tranquil alleys{end_bold} leading to {start_bold}sun-kissed squares{end_bold}. Don't miss the {start_bold}local street markets{end_bold}, which sell everything from flowers to fish.
items.-1466824: Saint Malo's {start_bold}massive stone walls{end_bold} once sheltered a {start_bold}notorious pirate den{end_bold}. Where tourists now roam, corsairs would plot their next attack...
items.-1471697: Stay among the beautiful half-timber buildings of {start_bold}“Petite France”{end_bold} – a waterside neighborhood where medieval tanners, millers, and fishermen once lived and worked.
items.-1473166: The domes and turrets of {start_bold}churches{end_bold}, {start_bold}towers{end_bold}, and {start_bold}majestic townhouses{end_bold} tower above Toulouse’s old town. Pass by the impressive {start_bold}Place du Capitole{end_bold} and into streets full of warm buildings with picturesque balconies.
items.-1473290: {start_bold}Post-and-beam houses{end_bold}, dating from the 15th century, fill Tours old town’s maze of medieval streets. {start_bold}Place Plumereau{end_bold}, once home to the city’s hat market, is now filled with cozy cafés.
items.-1473937: Museums and churches are nestled among wooden-framed houses in Troyes’ old town. Stop by the {start_bold}Gothic cathedral{end_bold} and explore the {start_bold}Renaissance buildings{end_bold} found throughout the area.
items.-1658079: The core of Spanish-era Mexico City was built on the ruins of the {start_bold}Aztec capital of Tenochtitlan{end_bold}. The amazing legacies of both cultures are still visible today.
items.-1669612: The colonial-era "Centro" of Guadalajara features {start_bold}impressive churches{end_bold} and {start_bold}monuments{end_bold}, as well as {start_bold}notable murals by the famous artist Orozco{end_bold}.
items.-1669986: Guanajuato’s mining heritage is evident in its old town, where you can see its streets run into {start_bold}subterranean tunnels{end_bold}. Take in the {start_bold}colorful houses{end_bold}, {start_bold}grand Baroque mansions{end_bold} and {start_bold}squares{end_bold} as you wander.
items.-168008: Panama City’s old town is full of fascinating characters, as well as colorful buildings and cafes serving {start_bold}aromatic Geisha coffee{end_bold}. Stop by markets selling jewelry and {start_bold}vibrant textiles{end_bold}.
items.-1683102: Stones from {start_bold}Mayan ruins{end_bold} were reused to build the colonial {start_bold}cathedrals{end_bold} and {start_bold}palaces{end_bold} of Merida's old city.
items.-1685634: Shops and restaurants drawing on {start_bold}indigenous culture{end_bold} flourish in this charming district. The {start_bold}colonial-era buildings{end_bold} here are built from {start_bold}green volcanic stone{end_bold}.
items.-1690063: Puebla's historic center is an {start_bold}exotic blend of American and European architectural references{end_bold}. Many houses are covered in distinctive colored tiles called {start_bold}azulejos{end_bold}.
items.-1690669: Querétaro’s old town is a mix of alleys filled with shops selling {start_bold}local crafts{end_bold} like embroidered clothing and lace. {start_bold}Great squares{end_bold} and {start_bold}churches{end_bold} show off the city’s lavish architecture.
items.-1699222: San Miguel de Allende’s old town is filled with captivating, warm-colored churches, like the pink-tinted {start_bold}Parroquia{end_bold}. The {start_bold}"Jardín" square{end_bold} is where the locals eat, meet and gather to enjoy festivals.
items.-1707815: Veracruz’s old town comes alive in its {start_bold}Zócalo main square{end_bold}, where you might see some live music or dancing. Stop by the nearby {start_bold}cathedral{end_bold} before you try some of the region’s famous coffee.
items.-1736191: Luxembourg's old town has a dramatic and unique setting, with {start_bold}pastel buildings{end_bold} scattered between several {start_bold}cliffs and gorges{end_bold}.
items.-1746605: Enjoy famous {start_bold}Moselle wines{end_bold} in the perfect setting of {start_bold}romantic cobblestone streets{end_bold} and {start_bold}half-timber houses{end_bold}.
items.-1750167: A rococo-style town hall overlooks Bonn’s {start_bold}Marktplatz square{end_bold}. After you admire it, feel free to wander through its old town to see {start_bold}Beethoven’s birthplace{end_bold} at Bonngasse and browse fascinating {start_bold}old bookstores{end_bold}.
items.-1752234: The highlight of Bremen's historic center is its stunning {start_bold}15th-century town hall{end_bold}, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Pro tip: Some of the {start_bold}oldest wines in Germany{end_bold} are located in the building's cellar.

items.-658339: The old town of Ouro Preto is lined with {start_bold}shops selling jewelry and precious stones{end_bold}, fitting for a Gold Rush-era town. The center is also scattered with elaborate pieces by sculptor, {start_bold}Aleijadinho{end_bold}.
items.-659504: Paraty's {start_bold}whitewash colonial buildings{end_bold} stand in total contrast to the surrounding {start_bold}emerald rain forest{end_bold} and {start_bold}aquamarine ocean{end_bold}.
items.-661457: The old town of Petrópolis surrounds a {start_bold}Gothic cathedral{end_bold} and on its streets, you'll find Imperial-era buildings. Walk around to spot impressive homes and palaces, as well as the {start_bold}Imperial Museum{end_bold}.
items.-662356: Pirenópolis has a bright, lively old town with cobblsetone streets and traditional houses known as {start_bold}"casarões."{end_bold} It’s home to{start_bold} traditional restaurants{end_bold} and historic churches like {start_bold}Rosário de Meia Ponte{end_bold}.
items.-663509: A bustling area where {start_bold}extravagant neoclassical structures{end_bold} squeeze next to {start_bold}modernist office buildings{end_bold}.
items.-665520: Above its colored pavement tiles, Recife is dotted with museums celebrating {start_bold}local culture{end_bold}. The streets leading from {start_bold}Marco Zero Square{end_bold} are filled with lively bars and restaurants.
items.-667833: Experience Salvador's historic center, where {start_bold}pastel-hued houses and churches{end_bold} fill bustling neighborhoods rich in Afro-Brazilian heritage. It's also one of the oldest colonial cities in South America (founded 1549).
items.-676172: White-washed houses with colorful touches line the streets of Tiradentes, right by the golden {start_bold}Matriz Church{end_bold}. There are plenty of {start_bold}museums{end_bold} to discover and a beautiful square to watch the city pass by.
items.-735347: The "Kaleiçi," meaning "within the castle," is an {start_bold}ancient cluster of houses and monuments{end_bold} dating back to Roman times. The old buildings surround a {start_bold}turquoise, yacht-filled harbor{end_bold}.
items.-740501: The 13th-century capital of the Ottoman Empire, Bursa isn’t short on history. Its old town is filled with intricately designed {start_bold}mosques{end_bold}, traditional {start_bold}thermal baths{end_bold}, and a silk market, the {start_bold}Koza Han{end_bold}.
items.-755070: Discover Istanbul’s old town, which boasts more history than almost any other place in the world. Explore nearby icons like the {start_bold}Hagia Sophia{end_bold} and the {start_bold}Grand Bazaar{end_bold}.
items.-79996: Dubrovnik's famous old town is protected by {start_bold}turquoise waters{end_bold} and still intact {start_bold}16th-century fortifications{end_bold}. It really feels like another world – no wonder {start_bold}Game of Thrones{end_bold} films here regularly.
items.-814876: Athens' old town is nicknamed {start_bold}"the Neighborhood of the Gods"{end_bold} with good reason – its picture-perfect alleys are located directly under the {start_bold}Acropolis{end_bold}.
items.-820164: Chania's {start_bold}narrow alleys{end_bold} are lined with greenery and reveal a {start_bold}fascinating mix of Venetian and Turkish architecture{end_bold}, reflecting the area's rich and complex history.
items.-824497: From {start_bold}Palamidi Castle{end_bold}, check out Nafplion’s fascinating old town all the way down to the sea. Follow its streets downhill, walk past {start_bold}Venetian residences{end_bold} and traces of the {start_bold}Ottoman era{end_bold}, and enjoy plenty of bars and restaurants.
items.-827465: Rethymno's charming old town is an {start_bold}interesting mix of Venetian and Turkish influences{end_bold}. Many buildings' upper stories stretch out over the street with {start_bold}unique wooden parapets{end_bold}.
items.-837298: Plovdiv is full of Roman ruins, like the {start_bold}Odeon{end_bold} and a 2nd-century {start_bold}stadium{end_bold}. Art galleries, old mosaics, and the towering minaret of {start_bold}Dzhumaya Mosque{end_bold} will definitely grab your attention.
items.-840999: One highlight of the old town is the massive {start_bold}Bratislava Castle{end_bold}, built more than 500 years ago. It still faithfully guards the area's winding medieval alleys.
items.-843247: Košice’s old town is famous for its {start_bold}cafe culture{end_bold} and terraces that look over impressive landmarks. Must-sees include the {start_bold}Gothic St. Elisabeth Cathedral{end_bold} and the fancy façade of the {start_bold}town hall{end_bold}.
items.-850553: Explore Budapest's Old Town – home to famous attractions like {start_bold}Buda Castle{end_bold} and the {start_bold}Fisherman's Bastion{end_bold}.
items.-85142: Seen from above, Korcula's old town is a tiny jewel of {start_bold}orange roofs and stone houses{end_bold}, clustered next to the {start_bold}beautiful waters of the Adriatic{end_bold}.
items.-852573: Yellow, red, and orange buildings add a splash of color to Eger’s old town. Try spotting the {start_bold}basilica{end_bold}, enjoy the charming {start_bold}Dobó Square{end_bold}, and stop by a street-side bar to sip on the city’s {start_bold}famous red wine{end_bold}, Egri Bikavér.
items.-85411: Kotor's old town is nestled in a stunning setting, a rocky bend in the Adriatic some call {start_bold}"the southernmost fjord in Europe."{end_bold} Don't miss the {start_bold}Venetian-era city fortifications{end_bold}.
items.-87271: Ljubljana's old town might be tiny, but it has a lot to offer. Don't miss the {start_bold}"Triple" and "Dragon" bridges{end_bold} over the {start_bold}Ljubljanica river{end_bold}, then climb {start_bold}Castle Hill for an unforgettable view{end_bold}.
items.-89574: Mostar’s beautiful old bridge, {start_bold}Stari Most{end_bold}, is the star of this picturesque old town. Terracotta roofs and the minaret of the {start_bold}Mehmed Paša Mosque{end_bold} overlook the banks of the beautiful Neretva River.
items.-901202: The old town's {start_bold}beautiful squares{end_bold} are perfect for sipping a coffee and chatting with the locals.
items.-906319: Colonia del Sacramento's old town is scattered with building built between the 17th and 19th centuries. Discover the {start_bold}city gates{end_bold}, {start_bold}Uruguay’s oldest church{end_bold}, and {start_bold}Calle de los Suspiros{end_bold} – a charming old street overlooking the sea.
items.-907764: The old town is nestled in a narrow piece of land reaching out into the sea, with {start_bold}crumbling colonial monuments{end_bold} and a {start_bold}buzzing nightlife{end_bold}.
items.-92761: There are tons of treasures hidden in Porec's historic center. Don't miss the {start_bold}Euphrasian Basilica{end_bold}, with its jewel-studded {start_bold}Byzantine mosaics{end_bold} around 1,500 years old.
items.-932573: Quito's historic center is one of the {start_bold}most well-preserved old towns in all of Latin America{end_bold}. Indigenous traditions influence the Colonial architecture here.
items.-93462: In Pula’s picturesque old town, the {start_bold}Roman amphitheater{end_bold} is one of the best preserved in the world. Explore the marketplace and look out for more Roman ruins, like the {start_bold}Temple of Augustus{end_bold}.
items.-94604: Circled by the Adriatic Sea, Rovinj old town’s buildings date back to {start_bold}Venetian times{end_bold}, featuring incredible orange, yellow, and terracotta colors. Don't miss out on {start_bold}St. Euphemia Church{end_bold} and its impressive views.
items.-94996: {start_bold}Church spires{end_bold} and {start_bold}minarets{end_bold} mix in Sarajevo's old town, a fascinating mix of Ottoman, Austro-Hungarian, Slavic, and Jewish influences.
items.-95841: This neighborhood has been {start_bold}Skopje's shopping center{end_bold} for an astounding 800 years. Mosques and Turkish baths surround a {start_bold}still-bustling covered bazaar.{end_bold}
items.-96492: Split's old town has {start_bold}the world's most well-preserved Roman palace{end_bold}, built 1,600 years ago for the emperor Diocletian. The former palace now shelters shops, restaurants, and even private houses.
items.-98777: Trogir's old town is a beautiful mix: {start_bold}fairy-tale medieval walls{end_bold} mingling with {start_bold}palm trees{end_bold}. Go exploring!
items.generic: The historic center – featuring picturesque alleys, ancient buildings, and impressive monuments.
